alerts.reason: Oil States’ Q2 consolidated revenue grew just 1%, while product revenue fell 6% on lower perforating-product demand and shipment timing (A, C). The $338 million offshore backlog could keep Q3 above −5%, but delayed shipments and continued demand weakness could push total revenue growth to −5% or lower in Q4 (B, C).

IDEX’s reported net sales grew 6% in Q2 versus 9% for the first half, indicating a slowdown. Pricing supported all segments while weaker Health & Science Technologies volumes partially offset those gains (A, D). I forecast Q3 growth stays above −5%, with a Q4 crossing if volume losses deepen as the benefit from pricing fades.

Software’s revenue share rose from 86% to 88%, implying a steeper decline outside software (A). I forecast Q3 stays narrowly above −5%, with modest further weakness enough for a Q4 crossing.

Spirit’s Q2 revenue grew 4.8% because traffic rose 13.1% despite a 7.4% yield decline. Capacity grew faster than traffic at 17.4%, and load factor fell 3.1 percentage points (A, B). I forecast traffic growth keeps Q3 above −5%, but continued yield pressure could push Q4 revenue growth to −5% or lower if traffic growth slows.
